key_insight: LLM scientific claim verifiers can reach the same verdict for different underlying interpretations, so the interpretation itself should be made explicit alongside the label.
engineering_relevance: For AI materials-science workflows, exposing and tracking claim interpretations can improve auditability, reproducibility, and tool-use decisions in automated literature verification.
method: Built a 9-field Claim Card to record a verifier’s interpretation before evidence gathering, marking each field as stated, inferred, or default.
Ran a GPT-5.4 agent 5 times on each of 60 expert-labeled materials-science and biomedical claims in three settings: with a card, without a card, and with a frozen card.
Tested how deliberate edits to one frozen-card field (quantifier/threshold) changed verdicts and, for 24 materials-science claims, downstream computational tool queries.
evidence_signal: Across 900 runs, over 40% of card fields were not stated, and adding a card increased GPT-5.4 tokens and time by about 10% without measurably changing agreement with expert labels; changing one interpretation field altered verdicts on about one-third of claims.
watch_item: The study uses one agent setup and a modest claim set, so results may not generalize to other models, domains, or benchmark annotation practices.
paper_title: Same Claim, Different Interpretations: How LLM Agents Resolve Ambiguity in Scientific Claims
